transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you for seeing me. Um, I guess I'm just here because... well, I've been having a little trouble focusing at work lately. It's probably nothing major, but, um, I'm a therapist, so I really need to be present for my clients, you know? But recently, I've just been... losing track of what they're saying sometimes. And I catch myself rereading the same chart notes over and over. I even freeze up on simple decisions that used to be second nature. I hope that makes sense? I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job for them, and this foggy feeling is getting in the way a bit.
Have you been feeling down, sad, or have you lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

Um, I wouldn't necessarily say I'm feeling sad, exactly. I always try to keep a good attitude, you know? But... I guess I have been a little less engaged with my hobbies lately. 

I feel kind of guilty even admitting this, but my guitar has just been sitting in the corner gathering dust. And, um, I keep bailing on my soccer team and my volunteer shifts at the shelter. I really hate letting people down, so I feel awful about it. I still try to force myself to do things I usually love, like cooking or going for a hike, but... I don't know, it just feels like I'm going through the motions. Like there's no real point to it right now. 

I hope I'm explaining that right? I'm sure it's just a temporary rut or something, right?
Have you been feeling unusually tired or have you noticed a lack of energy, even if you’ve gotten enough rest?

Um, well, I guess I have been a little tired. But I know everyone gets tired, right? I really don't want to sound lazy, and I'm definitely still trying my best at work. 

It's just... lately, even if I sleep okay, just doing the small stuff—like taking a shower, or driving to the clinic, or finishing up my paperwork—it takes so much effort. It feels almost like... like I'm dragging around a backpack full of bricks all day. I'm really trying to just push through it so I don't fall behind or let my clients down. 

I hope that doesn't sound like I'm just making excuses? I'm sure it's just a phase and I just need to try a little harder to get my energy up. Does that sound normal to you?
Do you find yourself feeling overly worried or anxious about things, especially at work or in your daily life?

Um, well... I wouldn't say I'm *overly* worried. I mean, I care a lot about my job, and I really want to make sure I'm doing right by my clients, so I guess I do think about work quite a bit when I'm at home. But I wouldn't call it anxiety, really. 

I just want to be prepared and do a good job, you know? I try to stay positive and keep things in perspective. I don't want to come across like I'm complaining or like I can't handle the stress, because I know I can. It's just... maybe I'm overthinking things a little bit right now because I've been so tired? But I'm definitely not walking around in a panic all the time or anything like that. That's a pretty normal way to feel when you have a job where people rely on you, isn't it?
Have you noticed that things you used to find enjoyable or pleasurable don’t seem to bring you the same satisfaction anymore?

Um, well, I think I kind of mentioned this a little bit earlier when we talked about my hobbies? But... I wouldn't say they don't bring me satisfaction anymore. I mean, I still really love playing music and being active. I'm definitely not numb to it or anything. 

When I actually force myself to get out there and do it, I still think it's nice. It's really just that... getting the energy to start is the hard part right now, like I was saying. I don't want it to sound like I'm ungrateful for the good things in my life, because I'm really not. I still smile and try to have a good time when I'm around people. 

So... no, I don't think I've lost the ability to enjoy things, exactly. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you experienced periods where you felt down or sad most of the day, nearly every day?

Um, well... I wouldn't really say I've been sad most of the day. I mean, I have my moments, just like anyone else, right? But I really try my best to keep a smile on my face, especially at work. I don't want my clients or my coworkers to think I'm bringing them down or anything. 

I guess I've just been feeling a little more... flat? Or maybe just worn out, like we were talking about earlier. But I'm definitely not crying all the time or sitting around feeling sorry for myself. I really try to focus on the positive things and just keep moving forward. 

I mean, everyone has a few off days here and there, don't they? I just want to make sure I'm not making a bigger deal out of things than I should be. Am I explaining that okay?
Have you noticed any trouble with your thinking, like difficulty concentrating, making decisions, or remembering things lately?

Um, well... I guess maybe a little bit? But I don't want it to sound like I'm completely losing my mind or failing at my job, because I'm really trying hard not to let it affect my clients. 

It's just... lately, I've noticed I'm having a little trouble keeping my head completely clear at work. Like, sometimes I'll kind of lose track of what a client is saying for a second, or I'll catch myself rereading the same chart note a few times before it actually sinks in. And sometimes I'll just sort of freeze up on really simple decisions that I used to handle without even thinking about it. 

But I'm sure it's just because I'm so tired, right? I mean, it's not like I'm making huge mistakes or putting anyone at risk. I really care about my job, and I'm doing everything I can to stay on top of things. I just... I hope that doesn't make me sound incompetent. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture.
Have you felt like nothing gives you pleasure or makes you look forward to doing it, even the things you used to really enjoy?

Um, well... I know I said earlier that I still like my hobbies, and I really do want to! I just... I don't want you to think I'm completely giving up on everything, because I'm trying. 

But I guess if I'm being completely honest, my guitar has just sort of been sitting in the corner lately. And... well, I've been bailing on my soccer games and my shifts at the animal shelter, which I feel terrible about because I know they rely on me. I just tell them I'm too busy with work. 

Even when I do try to force myself to do things, like cooking a nice meal or going for a hike, it just sort of feels like I'm going through the motions? Like there's no real point to it right now. But I'm sure that's just a phase, right? I mean, everyone gets into a funk sometimes where they just want to stay home. I'm sure I'll bounce back and get back to all of it soon. I just hope I don't sound like I'm just being lazy... is that what it sounds like?
Would you say that you’re no longer getting any pleasure or enjoyment out of things that you used to really like doing?

Um, I know we just touched on this, and I really don't want to sound like a broken record or like I'm just whining... I'm really trying my best to stay active. 

But yeah, I guess I'd have to say the enjoyment just isn't there right now. Like I mentioned, my guitar is just collecting dust in the corner. And I keep making up excuses to get out of my soccer games and my volunteer shifts at the shelter. I hate doing that because I don't want to let anyone down, but I just can't seem to find the energy or the... I don't know, the spark for it? 

And even when I do force myself to do something, like trying to cook a nice dinner or going for a hike, it just feels like I'm going through the motions. There's just no point to it, you know? It doesn't give me that good feeling it used to. But I'm sure it's just temporary, right? I'm sure I'll get back to normal soon. Does that make sense, though? I just want to make sure I'm answering your question right.
Would you say that you’re not getting any enjoyment at all out of things you used to really like doing?

I know you're just trying to be thorough, and I'm really sorry if I'm not explaining myself well enough... I feel like I keep repeating myself, and I don't want to waste your time. 

But yes, to answer your question... I guess I'm really not getting any enjoyment out of things right now. Like I was saying about the guitar just sitting there, and how I keep making up excuses to skip soccer and the animal shelter. I just feel so guilty about it, because I don't want you to think I'm the kind of person who just abandons their commitments. I really am trying. 

It's just that even when I push myself to do things I normally love, like cooking or hiking, it just feels so empty. Like I'm just checking a box, and there's no real point to it anymore. It's really frustrating, and I hope I don't sound like a lost cause. I'm doing my best to stay positive about it. Am I giving you the information you need? I just want to make sure I'm being helpful.
